ratings.note: Common keyboard, dialog, live-region and state findings fail the skill's own lint on most runs, forcing a hand edit of tool-generated text every time and teaching agents to override a gate that is meant to be trusted.
Every rater and verifier packet carries paths with an unstated base, so fresh subagents waste reads on every run and may silently rate without seeing the screenshots the ratings should rest on.
Agents waste reads hunting for the schema on most runs, and a careful agent can find it by searching, but one that gives up may write output that does not match the schema.
Without a history action the probes cannot test the classic Back-button exit, so an agent either gathers evidence outside the skill or leaves a common defect class untested without saying so.

Every run with journeys hands heuristic evaluators the correct path and the avoided hints, silently priming them and inflating detection counts and agreement, which undermines the evaluator independence the report's confidence rests on.

Multi-role runs routinely leave the same problem listed several times because the merge matches exact routes, inflating counts and splitting one well-supported problem into many weaker-looking copies that crowd out the rest.

Whenever a second rating batch is built, first-batch ratings are silently decoded onto the wrong findings, corrupting severities with no warning, and only an agent who already suspects the hazard avoids it.

A bare empty queue invites a false 'nothing to fix' conclusion when the audit was simply never merged or promoted, and although a careful agent diagnoses it, the tool knows the cause and stays silent.
Verifier split requests are occasional and the manual route of new candidates, re-merge and re-verification works, but it costs effort each time and hand-edited JSON risks losing provenance.
